title: Building a shared fantasy stock market with Astra in Codex — gameplay and development notes
author: enmotent
selftext:
I built HypeStreet, a free browser game where players trade AI models and pop-culture figures with play money.



Astra helped implement persistent accounts, the shared market, trade confirmations, portfolios, and the leaderboard. I also used it to write tests for duplicate trade requests and concurrent spending, then iterate on the homepage through browser checks. I reviewed the results and directed follow-up changes; this wasn’t a one-prompt build.



Gameplay: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8JQF-Mi5zZA](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8JQF-Mi5zZA)

The recording uses local demo data, not live-player activity.



Play: [https://hypestreet.io](https://hypestreet.io) — account required to trade, no real money or cash-out.



The launch is on Product Hunt today: [https://www.producthunt.com/products/hypestreet?launch=hypestreet](https://www.producthunt.com/products/hypestreet?launch=hypestreet)



For others building multiplayer games with AI: how are you checking that concurrent actions can’t corrupt player balances or shared state?
